questions.explanation:
The reaction proceeds via an electrophilic addition mechanism.

First, the alkene is protonated by $H^+$ from $HBr$ according to Markovnikov's rule. The proton adds to the terminal $CH_2$ carbon to generate the more stable tertiary carbocation, the 2-cyclobutylpropan-2-yl cation.

The four-membered cyclobutane ring is highly strained. To relieve this angle strain, the intermediate undergoes a ring expansion. A C-C bond of the cyclobutane ring migrates to the adjacent positively charged carbon. This expands the ring to a five-membered cyclopentane ring, resulting in the formation of a secondary carbocation, the 2,2-dimethylcyclopentyl cation.

To achieve greater stability, this secondary carbocation undergoes a 1,2-methyl shift from the adjacent quaternary carbon. This rearrangement yields a more stable tertiary carbocation, the 1,2-dimethylcyclopentyl cation.

Finally, the nucleophilic bromide ion ($Br^-$) attacks this tertiary carbocation to form the major product, 1-bromo-1,2-dimethylcyclopentane.

The structure of 1-bromo-1,2-dimethylcyclopentane corresponds to option (4). !
